s1_spec.q: Why can the harness serve only one repository today?
s1_spec.a: It finds its configuration, its store and the role-context briefing by looking next to its own code, so it is wired to the repository it lives in.

s1_spec.q: Which two groups does the problem affect?
s1_spec.a: The operator, who runs it against two repositories and keeps two drifting copies; and anyone who adopts the factory for a new project.

s1_spec.q: What does each target repository's .factory/ folder hold?
s1_spec.a: The repository's configuration, its briefing, the harness revision it has accepted (the lock), and its records (the store).

s1_spec.q: What exactly does the harness lock pin, and why not the checkout's HEAD?
s1_spec.a: The last commit touching factory/, bin/factory, agents/, pyproject.toml or uv.lock. A HEAD lock would refuse after every store or document commit in this repo.

s1_spec.q: When does the harness check the lock?
s1_spec.a: Only when the command uses the instance's own store; a run with FACTORY_STATE pointing elsewhere (as every test does) is not checked.

s1_spec.q: What happens when no instance is found?
s1_spec.a: The command is refused and nothing is written; there is no fallback to an instance of the harness's own.

s1_spec.q: Where are tickets merged, and where does the factory run from?
s1_spec.a: Merged in the dev checkout ~/dev/spec-factory on main; run from the runtime, a detached worktree at ~/dev/spec-factory-harness.

s1_spec.q: How and when is the runtime upgraded?
s1_spec.a: When no ticket is in flight: git -C ~/dev/spec-factory-harness checkout --detach <sha>, then --accept-harness <sha> in each instance that uses it.

s1_spec.q: What happens to hand-written notes on the preamble's protected-path line?
s1_spec.a: They are lost, because the line is generated from instance.yaml's globs; such notes belong in context.md.

s1_spec.q: Is moving green (the Nanobot fork) onto the new layout part of this change?
s1_spec.a: No; it is a separate, later ticket.

s2_pr.q: What new file does the change add, and how big is it?
How does the rule reach every role?
s2_pr.a: A line in the shared preamble's OUTPUT block carries a {writing standard} placeholder, which fill_preamble replaces at run start with the path of docs/writing.md in the running harness checkout.

s2_pr.q: Which spec sections does the critic's rubric 6 now cover?
s2_pr.a: Problem, Evidence, Open questions, Decisions and Operator steps.

s2_pr.q: How severe is a finding from the new code-reviewer check 8?
How many tests ran before and after, and why the difference?
s2_pr.a: 121 before, 126 after: the new test file adds 5 tests.

s2_pr.q: Which agents do not see the new rule?
s2_pr.a: Agents that use the registered role agents from the agents/ templates, which this change does not touch; only runs that read system-prompt.txt get it.

s2_pr.q: When do agents start seeing the change?
s2_pr.a: Only after the operator moves the runtime to a revision containing this commit and accepts it.
Whether a live critic actually blocks on an unglossed term in an Evidence paragraph; that needs a model run after the upgrade.

s2_pr.q: What stands in for the request's checks-in-flight example, and why?
s2_pr.a: A real escalation from run-0062-verifier, used in rule 7, because the checks-in-flight escalation could not be found.

s2_pr.q: Was any existing test assertion removed or loosened?

s3_escalation.q: What is the conflict, in one sentence?
s3_escalation.a: Spec part C.2's refusal when the lock is missing makes an existing test fail, and the sub-ticket forbids changing tests.

s3_escalation.q: Which test fails, and where did it come from?

s3_escalation.a: It builds an instance directory alt with only instance.yaml and context.md, no harness.lock, then runs config on that instance's own store, which C.2 now refuses (exit 2).

s3_escalation.q: What resolution is proposed, and was it tried?
s3_escalation.a: Add the test to Tests to change with one line copying the target's harness.lock into alt; it was applied temporarily, passed, and reverted.

s3_escalation.q: What alternative was rejected, and why?
s3_escalation.a: Exempting config from the lock, because it contradicts C.2's 'every command except init and paths'.
Informational: four NEW criteria passed vacuously at base; not a spec defect.

s3_escalation.q: What does the escalation need from a human?
s3_escalation.a: A ruling: add the test to Tests to change, or amend C.2.
